comparisons.interpretation: Garza emphasizes public-health interventions, reduced incarceration and gun-violence prevention; Sylestine emphasizes jury trials, survivor trust and backlog reduction. Both mention survivors, so that concern is not assigned exclusively to one candidate.

Incumbent Garza presents progress that should continue; challenger Sylestine presents a system needing restored function and balance. The contrast concerns their campaign narratives, not an independent finding about the office's performance.
Both support the New York Health Act. Different backgrounds and rhetorical styles do not establish a disagreement on this named healthcare proposal.
Both affirm Good Cause Eviction protections in their own responses.
Both support sex-work decriminalization; the shorter response is not treated as opposition or weaker commitment.
Both answer yes to unarmed mental-health crisis response. This specific agreement does not imply identical positions on every policing issue.

Forrest emphasizes grassroots movement-building and solidarity; Alabi emphasizes practical, responsive leadership beyond ideology. Their common support for several named policies is preserved alongside this messaging contrast.
